svg.title: How a usability lesson is made: every grounding is charted once, so the next vessel sails clear
svg.desc: Five stations left to right. The Grounding: a ship strikes a rock, someone is failed by a surface. The Logbook: it is written down once with evidence, by the skill log-usability-finding. The Chart: the keeper rates it and distils one reusable rule. The Lighthouse: the rule is published as a plugin whose guard warns on its own. The Next Vessel: warned before it nears the rock, and able to ask first with the skill usability-lessons. Below, the four skills a crew calls: usability-init declares a repository, usability-lessons reads the lessons for a surface, log-usability-finding records a failure, and usability-setup points a repository's docs at the ledger. Only usability-lessons ships in the public plugin.

g.text: How a usability lesson is made
Every grounding is charted once, so the next vessel sails clear.
FIVE STATIONS · FOUR SKILLS · ONE KEEPER
Someone is failed by a surface.
Its guard warns on its own.
THE CREW'S CALLS · THE FOUR SKILLS YOU TYPE
Once per repo: declares it to the ledger.
Reads the chart before you sail.
Before work: the lessons for one surface.
Writes the grounding in the logbook.
After a failure: evidence and a lesson.
Optional: points your docs at the ledger.

svg.text: The point: no one runs aground twice in the same place.
